Assignment Title: Debugging_Real-time Leaderboard System   TreeMap

Assignment Question:
You are developing a real-time Leaderboard System for a multiplayer gaming platform. The system uses a Java TreeMap to automatically keep players sorted by their scores in descending order. When a player completes a match, the system retrieves their current score, updates it by adding the points earned in the match, and updates the leaderboard. However, the QA team noticed a critical bug: after several match updates, players with updated scores are completely missing when searching the leaderboard, or they appear out of order. Your task is to find the bug in the code, fix it, and ensure the scores update and sort correctly.

Input Format:
 
·       The first line contains an integer N, representing the number of initial players.
·       The next N lines each contain a String (player name) and an Integer (initial score), separated by a space.
·       The next line contains a String (the player who just finished a match) and an Integer (the match points to add), separated by a space.
·       The final line contains a String representing a player name to look up on the leaderboard after the match update.
 
Output Format:
 
·       The first line prints the updated score of the searched player (or "Player not found").
·       The subsequent lines print the entire leaderboard in descending order of scores, formatted as Name: Score.
 Sample Input
3
Alpha 100
Beta 250
Gamma 150
Alpha 200
Alpha
 
Sample Output:
Alpha's updated score: 300
Leaderboard:
Alpha: 300
Beta: 250
Gamma: 150
